"'''Burning Heart'''" is a song by American rock band [[Survivor (band)|Survivor]]. It appeared in the [[1985 in film|1985]] film ''[[Rocky IV]]'' and on its [[Rocky IV: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack|soundtrack album]]; the film's star [[Sylvester Stallone]] personally commissioned the song.<ref>{{cite book |first=Alex P. |last=King |title=Hit-parade — 20 ans de tubes |publisher=Pascal |year=2004 |place=Paris |page=342 |language=fr |isbn=2-35019-009-9}}</ref> The [[Single (music)|single]] peaked at number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart for two weeks; it was the biggest hit the band had with [[Jimi Jamison]] on lead vocals. It was also a hit internationally, topping the charts of Belgium and Switzerland and entering the top 10 in several other European countries.

"Burning Heart" is a song by American rock band Survivor. It appeared in the 1985 film Rocky IV and on its soundtrack album; the film's star Sylvester Stallone personally commissioned the song. The single peaked at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart for two weeks; it was the biggest hit the band had with Jimi Jamison on lead vocals. It was also a hit internationally, topping the charts of Belgium and Switzerland and entering the top 10 in several other European countries.

sections.heading: Content
sections.wikitext: "Burning Heart", which is about an "all or nothing" battle, was inspired by the [[Cold War]],<ref>''Billboard'', 2 November 1985, S. 72 [https://books.google.com/books?id=RyQEAAAAMBAJ&q=survivor&pg=PA72 "burning heart" cold war&f=false Google Books]</ref> as shown by lyrics such as "Is it East versus West?"<ref>Daniel S. Papp: "Contemporary international relations: frameworks for understanding", Macmillan, 1988, S. 15 [https://archive.org/details/contemporaryinte00dani <!-- quote=survivor "burning heart" Is it East versus West?. --> Internet Archive]</ref> and "Can any nation stand alone?" The [[Communism|Communist]] East versus [[Capitalism|Capitalist]] West conflict is reflected in the film by the fight in the boxing ring between [[Rocky Balboa|Rocky]] and [[Ivan Drago]].
sections.text: "Burning Heart", which is about an "all or nothing" battle, was inspired by the Cold War, as shown by lyrics such as "Is it East versus West?" and "Can any nation stand alone?" The Communist East versus Capitalist West conflict is reflected in the film by the fight in the boxing ring between Rocky and Ivan Drago.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video for "Burning Heart" features [[Survivor (band)|Survivor]] giving a concert, mixed with scenes from the film ''[[Rocky IV]]''.<ref>[http://www.myvideo.de/watch/5471752/Survivor_Burning_Heart Music video in Myvideo.de] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229080115/http://www.myvideo.de/watch/5471752/Survivor_Burning_Heart |date=December 29, 2010 }}</ref> A version with only the band (no movie footage) also exists, available on YouTube.
sections.text: The music video for "Burning Heart" features Survivor giving a concert, mixed with scenes from the film Rocky IV. A version with only the band (no movie footage) also exists, available on YouTube.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext: In ''[[Smash Hits]]'', [[Janice Long]] wrote, "Watch out, "[[Eye of the Tiger]]" Mark 2. It sounds like exactly the same backing track, and it's from ''Rocky IV''. I think we could live without this record."<ref>{{cite magazine| magazine= [[Smash Hits]] | title=Singles|author=Janice Long|date=29 January 1986 |page=47}}</ref>
